events.title: The Senate condemns Catiline's fellow conspirators
events.description: After Cicero's fourth speech against Catiline, and Cato's demand for severity, the Senate voted to execute five conspirators without trial. Cicero was hailed as saviour of the Republic but later exiled for it.

events.title: The Fourth Council of Toledo opens under Isidore of Seville
events.description: All the bishops of Hispania gathered at the church of Saint Leocadia in Toledo for the council convened by the Visigothic king Sisenand, over which Isidore of Seville probably presided. It decreed a uniform liturgy throughout the kingdom.

events.title: An earthquake in the Jordan Rift Valley devastates the Levant
events.description: An earthquake in the Jordan Rift Valley, estimated at above magnitude 7.0, caused extreme devastation across the Levant and a tsunami along the Mediterranean coast. At least 70,000 people were killed.
events.html: An earthquake in the Jordan Rift Valley, estimated at above magnitude 7.0, caused extreme devastation across the Levant and a tsunami along the Mediterranean coast. At least 70,000 people were killed.

events.title: John II creates the first franc
events.description: By an ordinance issued at Compiègne, the newly released John II of France created the gold franc, partly to raise his ransom. The franc remained the name of French currency until the euro.

events.title: Pope Innocent VIII issues a bull against witchcraft
events.description: The bull Summis desiderantes affectibus authorised the inquisitors Heinrich Kramer and Jacob Sprenger to pursue witches in Germany. Kramer printed it with his Malleus Maleficarum, fuelling later witch hunts.

events.title: Frederick the Great routs an Austrian army at Leuthen
events.description: West of Breslau in Silesia, Frederick the Great used the oblique order of attack to rout an Austrian army about twice the size of his own under Prince Charles of Lorraine. The victory restored Prussian control of Silesia.

events.title: Mozart dies in Vienna aged 35
events.description: Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart died after a short illness, leaving his Requiem unfinished. In a career of barely three decades he wrote more than 600 works, including The Marriage of Figaro and The Magic Flute.

events.title: Prohibition ends in the United States
events.description: Utah became the 36th state to ratify the 21st Amendment, repealing national Prohibition. The ban on alcohol had lasted almost 14 years and fed a boom in organised crime.
